tagline: Hotkey → record → Whisper → paste at cursor

pricing.freeTier: The free plan caps dictation at 2,000 words per week on desktop.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Desktop: 2,000 dictated words/week; iPhone: 1,000 words/week; Android: unlimited words; recordings under 5 minutes do not count.
tiers.notes: Meeting-notetaker weekly cap is mentioned but its number is not public.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited dictation across supported devices; 1 paid user.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom paid-user count; admin seats are free and no minimum seat count is published.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Desktop 2,000 words/week; iPhone 1,000 words/week; Android unlimited; recordings under 5 minutes do not count.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (20% off); no commitment and cancel anytime
pricing.hiddenCosts: Enterprise admin seats are free, but regular users are billed; volume discounts are custom. Students and educators with accepted .edu eligibility can receive Pro free, while nonprofit discounts are custom.

verdictSummary: Hotkey → record → Whisper → paste at cursor. One of the most-cloned apps of the trend for a reason.
name: Wispr Flow
notes: Hotkey → record → Whisper → paste at cursor. One of the most-cloned apps of the trend for a reason.

alternatives.name: FluidVoice
alternatives.desc: Local Mac dictation with on-device cleanup and no weekly word allowance.

facts.install: Signed macOS download or Homebrew cask
facts.engines: Local engines include NVIDIA Nemotron Speech, Parakeet Flash/TDT, Cohere Transcribe models, Apple Speech, and Whisper; optional cleanup can use the local Fluid Intelligence model or OpenAI, Groq, and custom compatible endpoints.
facts.dataFormat: Transcripts, optional history, recordings, dictionaries, and settings stay on the Mac; API keys use Keychain, and optional cloud cleanup sends text to the selected provider. Exports can be created locally.
facts.gapVsPaid: It is limited to macOS and requires local model downloads or provider configuration, rather than Wispr Flow's managed cross-platform transcription and adaptive formatting.
facts.setupBlocker: It requires macOS 15, microphone and Accessibility permissions, and a model download; Intel Macs are limited to the Whisper path.

alternatives.name: Handy
alternatives.desc: The literal replacement: press, record, transcribe locally, paste.

facts.install: DMG, MSI, deb, rpm, or AppImage
facts.engines: Local Whisper Small, Medium, Turbo, and Large models; NVIDIA Parakeet v3; Silero VAD; optional cleanup through local or configured LLM and OpenRouter-compatible providers.
facts.dataFormat: History is stored in a local SQLite history.db database and recordings as local WAV files; configured cleanup providers receive the transcript sent to them.
facts.gapVsPaid: Handy can reproduce hotkey-to-cursor dictation, but its local cleanup and app-context adaptation are less automatic and consistent than Wispr Flow's managed service.
facts.setupBlocker: The first run needs microphone and text-injection permissions plus a model download; on Linux, automatic insertion may require xdotool, wtype, or dotool depending on the desktop.

alternatives.name: Muesli
alternatives.desc: A very fast local hold-to-talk loop on Apple Silicon, with optional cleanup and no account.

facts.install: Signed macOS DMG or Homebrew cask
facts.engines: Local speech models include Parakeet variants, Cohere Transcribe, Nemotron, SenseVoice, Qwen3 ASR, Indic ASR, Gemma, and Whisper; cleanup and summaries can use OpenAI, OpenRouter, ChatGPT OAuth, Ollama, LM Studio, or custom endpoints.
facts.dataFormat: The app stores its library in a local SQLite database under the macOS Application Support folder and recordings on disk; optional iCloud sync is text-only and recordings do not sync. Exports include PDF, Markdown, and JSON.
facts.gapVsPaid: Muesli is Apple-silicon Mac-only and requires choosing local models or cleanup providers instead of offering Wispr Flow's uniform managed experience.
facts.setupBlocker: It requires Apple-silicon macOS 14.2 or later, microphone and Accessibility permissions, and at least one local model download or external provider configuration.

alternatives.name: OpenWhispr
alternatives.desc: Hotkey, local model, cleaned text at the cursor, plus searchable history and meeting capture.

facts.install: Native macOS, Windows, or Linux installer; optional account enables cloud services
facts.engines: Local Whisper, NVIDIA Parakeet, and llama.cpp-based processing; optional managed or bring-your-own-key cloud paths use providers such as OpenAI and Groq.
facts.dataFormat: Local mode stores transcriptions, notes, agent data, and preferences in a local SQLite database, with optional local recordings; cloud sync is optional, and cloud transcription audio is described as transient rather than retained.
facts.gapVsPaid: The free local mode gives up Wispr Flow's managed cloud speed, synchronized context, and zero-configuration cleanup unless the user adds keys or pays.
facts.setupBlocker: The free local path needs permissions and a model download; cloud-speed, synchronization, and some advanced AI conveniences require an account, provider key, or paid plan.

alternatives.name: Spokenly
alternatives.desc: Unlimited offline dictation on Mac, Windows, Linux and iPhone; managed cloud is optional.

facts.install: Native macOS, Windows, Linux, or iPhone app
facts.engines: Free local transcription uses Whisper and Parakeet; bring-your-own-key cloud options include OpenAI, Deepgram, and Groq, while Spokenly's managed cloud and AI cleanup are paid.
facts.dataFormat: Offline mode keeps audio and transcripts on the device; a selected cloud provider receives audio for cloud transcription and the provider's retention rules apply. Spokenly does not publish the local database or file format.
facts.gapVsPaid: The no-cost path is local transcription, while managed cloud processing, AI cleanup, and synchronization, the closest equivalents to Wispr Flow, are paid.
facts.setupBlocker: Local use needs microphone and Accessibility permissions plus a model download; BYOK cloud use requires creating and protecting a provider key.

alternatives.name: TypeNo
alternatives.desc: A deliberately tiny Mac app for hotkey, speech, transcription and paste.

facts.install: Download the signed and notarized macOS app, then install its separate local speech-engine dependencies
facts.engines: The local coli speech-recognition engine; the current public setup does not identify a supported cloud backend.
facts.dataFormat: It keeps no transcript history: captured audio is processed locally, the result is placed in the clipboard or active app, and downloaded model files live under ~/.coli/models.
facts.gapVsPaid: It has no smart rewriting, app context, glossary, history, or cross-device support, and its supposedly tiny install still needs Node.js, ffmpeg, npm, and a model.
facts.setupBlocker: Despite the polished app bundle, setup requires Node.js LTS, ffmpeg, a global npm install of @marswave/coli, and a separate model download.

alternatives.name: Vocalinux
alternatives.desc: Linux finally gets hold-to-talk dictation with an AppImage, Wayland support and no cloud alibi.

facts.install: Interactive shell installer, AppImage, or AUR package
facts.engines: whisper.cpp, OpenAI Whisper through PyTorch, VOSK, and Silero VAD, all running locally.
facts.dataFormat: Audio is processed in memory and discarded; configuration is stored as YAML under ~/.config/vocalinux, and the app intentionally has no transcript-history database.
facts.gapVsPaid: It is Linux-only and deliberately has no cleanup, app-context rewriting, transcript history, glossary, or cloud synchronization.
facts.setupBlocker: Linux text injection is the first snag: the user may need IBus, wtype, ydotool, or xdotool depending on Wayland or X11, in addition to downloading a model.

alternatives.name: Voquill
alternatives.desc: Wispr Flow without the meter: hotkey, local transcription, cleanup, glossary and paste.

facts.install: Native macOS, Windows, or Linux installer; on-premises deployment is also offered
facts.engines: Local Whisper; cloud or BYOK connections include Groq, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Azure, and compatible endpoints, with local or provider-backed cleanup.
facts.dataFormat: Local history, audio, settings, and encrypted keys live in a local SQLite database; optional cloud synchronization stores account, dictionary, and tone data in Firebase, while cloud audio is described as transient.
facts.gapVsPaid: Local mode needs a model and permissions, while the faster synchronized cloud experience closest to Wispr Flow requires an account, provider credentials, or payment.
facts.setupBlocker: Local use requires permissions and a model download; the smoother cloud transcription and sync path needs an account, provider credentials, or the paid service.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Aiko
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Still appears in old free-app lists; the current app is paid and the download is a trial.

rejectedAlternatives.name: FreeFlow
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The app is free, but the normal path still depends on a third-party API key; fully local means running your own model server.

rejectedAlternatives.name: VoiceInk
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Open-source code, paid official build; a non-builder does not get the app for free.

prompt:
Build me a system-wide AI dictation tool like Wispr Flow for macOS. Requirements:

- A background app with a global hotkey (hold-to-talk fn key or a chosen shortcut).
  While held: record the mic. On release: transcribe and paste.
- Transcribe with whisper.cpp locally (small or medium model), or the Groq/OpenAI
  Whisper API if a key exists in .env · pick per a config flag.
- Pipe the raw transcript through an LLM (key in .env) with a short prompt that
  removes filler words, fixes punctuation, and matches casing to dictation style.
- Insert the result at the current cursor position in whatever app has focus
  (simulate keystrokes or use the pasteboard + Cmd-V approach, restoring the
  previous clipboard afterwards).
- Show a tiny floating pill while recording so I know it's live.
- Menu bar toggle for on/off, launch at login, and a settings file for the hotkey.
- No accounts, no telemetry, works offline with the local model.
- README with the Accessibility/Input Monitoring permissions I need to grant.
